A/C Repair in Katy, TX, From the Old Rice Town to the Newest Subdivisions

Katy is a small city inside a very large suburb, and the house you live in may sit in Harris, Fort Bend or Waller County. Call the free line any hour to be put through to an independent, locally owned HVAC company that works in the Katy area.

A/C repair in Katy covers a lot of ground. The City of Katy grew up around a rail stop and rice farms, while the much larger Katy area around it is a spread of master-planned subdivisions, some built inside a federal flood reservoir. Here is what makes cooling and heating a Katy home different, and how one free call reaches a local company.

Houston Air & Heating does not fix air conditioners. Dial (832) 662-4107 and an automated assistant asks what you need and what is going wrong, then hands the call to an HVAC company in the Katy area that is independent and locally owned. It looks at the system, gives you its price and does the repair, and you pay it directly.

Katy: a railroad town that became a three county suburb

Settlers first called this stretch of coastal prairie Cane Island, after a creek full of cane, and by 1847 it was a stagecoach stop on the San Felipe Road. The town was platted in 1895, got its post office and its name in January 1896, and sat on the Missouri, Kansas and Texas rail line. Rice farming and rice mills carried it for decades. Katy did not incorporate until 1945.

Today the city counted 21,894 people in the 2020 census and reaches into Harris, Fort Bend and Waller counties. Most people with a Katy address actually live outside it. Cinco Ranch, for example, is an unincorporated community of nearly 17,000 people about 10 miles southeast of the city. That matters for permits, for which county handles flood questions and for who you call when something goes wrong.

Services Katy homeowners ask about

Most summer calls are plain AC repair: warm air, a unit that hums but will not start, or ice on the copper line. A system that quits on a holiday weekend is what emergency AC repair is for. And when the first cold front comes through, furnace repair takes over.

Katy homes and the Barker Reservoir

The Addicks and Barker reservoirs are federal flood control lakes that sit dry most of the time. During Hurricane Harvey in 2017 they filled, and some Katy area neighborhoods learned they were built inside the Barker flood pool.

What happened upstream

The Army Corps of Engineers kept the reservoir gates closed during the storm to hold water behind the dams. Water backed up onto private land, and Fort Bend County leaders named Canyon Gate, Kelliwood, Cinco Ranch and areas along Mason Road among the neighborhoods that flooded.

What a court found

In December 2019 a judge on the U.S. Court of Federal Claims ruled that the way the government built and ran the dams amounted to a taking of the upstream properties that flooded, which opened the door to compensation for owners.

What it means for your AC

If your home flooded then or since, a condenser or air handler that sat in water deserves a careful look, even if it seemed to run fine afterward. If you are replacing equipment, ask whether raising the condenser and air handler makes sense for your lot.

Growth, new houses and first replacements

Katy ISD shows how fast the area keeps filling in. Demographers reported that the district gained about 14,870 students, or 18.6 percent, over five years, more than any other Houston area district. Much of that growth is in the northwest part of the district, where master-planned communities such as Elyson and Cane Island are still being built.

That mix means a Katy street can hold a 40 year old house next to one that is two years old. Each has its own typical problems. In a brand new home, the builder's warranty may cover a system that never cooled one room properly, so read it before you pay for a repair. In a home from the 1990s or early 2000s, the original equipment has likely been replaced once already, and the ducts in a hot attic may be due for a check too.

Safe checks before you call

  • Thermostat. Set it to Cool, lower than the room is now, and put in fresh batteries when the display looks dim or blank.
  • Filter. A filter packed with dust can freeze the coil and stop the airflow. Swap it if you can see it is clogged.
  • Breaker. Reset a tripped AC breaker one time. A second trip means the circuit needs a professional.
  • Outdoor unit. Pull grass clippings, leaves and toys away from the condenser so it can breathe.
  • Water at the indoor unit. A full drain pan or a tripped float switch can shut the system down. Note it and tell the company.

Gas smell or carbon monoxide alarm? Gas service in the Katy area comes from either CenterPoint Energy or SiEnergy, depending on the address. If you smell gas, get everyone out, then call 911 and the gas company named on your bill from outside. If a carbon monoxide alarm sounds, leave the house and call 911.

Power, gas and permits for a Katy address

CenterPoint Energy owns the poles, wires and meters in the Katy area and handles outages. Katy is in the part of Texas with retail electric choice, so the company that bills you is the retail provider you picked, not CenterPoint. When the whole street goes dark, report it to CenterPoint. When only the AC is down, the problem is in the equipment or its circuit, which an HVAC company handles.

Inside the city limits, Katy's Permit and Building Services division handles permits and inspections. The city lists installing air conditioning and heating systems as work that needs a permit, has adopted the 2021 International Building Codes, and has mechanical contractors register with the city every year. Outside the city, different rules can apply depending on the county, so ask the company to spell out which permit, if any, your replacement needs and to list it on the quote.

Questions to ask a Katy HVAC company

  • What is your Texas ACR license number? Then check it on the state's license search before work starts.
  • Is my house inside Katy city limits? It decides whether the city permit applies.
  • Did this unit or its wiring ever sit in floodwater? Ask them to look, especially near the reservoirs.
  • Did you size the new system with a load calculation? A replacement should fit the house as it is now, not just copy the old tonnage.
  • What refrigerant does the new system use? New equipment has moved to newer refrigerants, and the indoor and outdoor parts must match.

Common questions

Can I get 24 hour AC repair in Katy, TX?

The line picks up every hour of every day and puts your call through to a local, independent HVAC company serving the Katy area. Whether that company can come out in the middle of the night, and what it charges for after hours work, is up to the company, so ask on the call.

My house flooded when the Barker Reservoir backed up. Is my AC still safe to run?

Do not assume it is. If water reached the outdoor unit, the indoor unit or the electrical disconnect, leave it off and have a technician inspect the wiring, controls and coil before it runs. Water and silt can cause trouble long after the house dries out.

Does Katy require a permit for a new AC system?

Inside Katy city limits, yes. The City of Katy lists installing air conditioning and heating systems among the work that needs a permit, and it asks contractors to register with the city. Many Katy addresses are outside the city, in unincorporated Harris, Fort Bend or Waller County, so ask the company which rules apply to your home and who pulls any permit.

Who handles a power outage in Katy?

CenterPoint Energy delivers electricity in the Katy area and handles outages and downed lines. The retail electric provider on your bill handles billing only. Neither one repairs air conditioners, so if the lights are fine but the AC is dead, call an HVAC company.

Should I replace my AC or keep repairing it?

It depends on what failed and how old the system is. A blown capacitor on a younger unit is usually a repair. A failed compressor, a leaking coil or a system using R-22, a refrigerant with no new U.S. production or imports since 2020, tilts the decision toward replacement. Ask for both options in writing.
